newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Record daily gain pushes Hungary to almost 5,000.
newsitem.headline: Record daily gain pushes Hungary to almost 5,000.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index powered ahead with its highest ever daily gain on Wednesday as it capitalised on fresh money flowing into the market following positive corporate news.
The BUX index surged 175.99 points to 4,925.25.

"The Hungarian market is still very much in focus," said Zsolt Katona of ING Barings. "Foreign fund managers have a lot of money to spend and are buying more stocks," he said, adding the funds favoured Hungary even at current price levels.
Traders said a catalyst to the surge was corporate news, including tax relief for chemicals firm Borsodchem.
As a result, several papers hit new records, traders said, adding that the dollar's strength was another factor pushing the market up.

Chemicals firm Borsodchem shares leapt almost 10 percent on tax relief news. The company's CEO confirmed to Reuters that they expected 50 or 100 percent tax relief for 1997, stemming from Hungary's tax regulations.
Borsodchem soared to a new record of 5,160 forints, up 445, while the other chemicals firm, TVK gained 115 forints to finish at 2,365, just below a new record of 2,370.
The 12 percent retail price increase for medicines, effective from today, had minor positive impact on pharmaceuticals stocks, but chemicals papers stole the show from them today, traders said.
A salesman said earlier today that he tracked a tendency among investors according to which they give more room to chemicals in their portfolio.
"The pharmaceuticals papers were the bourse's flagships during the whole of last year and the fact that there are minor changes in portfolios does not mean any selling wave in them," a salesman said.
"But if we look at the differentials between the price gains of chemicals and pharmaceuticals stocks since the beginning of the year, we can see this mild shift."
